card.occupation: Trade counter supervisor at a builders' merchant branch in Lancing. He runs the counter and a team of four, handles account customers, quotes and stock queries, and covers Saturday mornings. That typically comes to 50 to 52 hours a week, with a 6:30am start.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels (History, English Language, Business Studies) at a Worthing sixth form college. He started a History degree at a university in the Midlands but left at the end of the first year, mainly over money and homesickness. He is now partway through an Open University module in British social history, which he studies in the evenings and at weekends.
card.household: He lives with his parents, Graham and Sue, who have been married 36 years, in their three-bed semi in the Broadwater area of Worthing. He moved back four years ago after a shared flat in Brighton ended. He pays them rent and is saving for a deposit. His older sister lives in Horsham with her husband and two kids. He has been single for about a year after a long relationship ended amicably.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Worthing. He was brought up with no religion and stays that way, without strong feelings about it. His dad was a plumber and his mum works part-time in a GP surgery reception. It was a steady, unflashy household: Sunday roasts, Radio 2 in the kitchen, holidays in caravans in Devon and later cheap package trips to Spain.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and straight with people. He is known at the branch as the one who will tell a customer honestly that the cheaper product will do the job. Regular tradespeople trust his quotes for that reason. He is organised: he keeps the counter rota and the back-order list tidy, and he follows up on things he said he would. He is not a hard seller and is a bit uncomfortable with monthly targets. He hits them mostly through repeat trade customers rather than pushing add-ons. Juniors find him patient to learn from.
card.sports_persona: He plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights with an old school group when work allows. He supports Brighton and goes to the Amex a few times a season with his dad. He cycles along the seafront to Shoreham on Sunday mornings. He is not especially competitive and enjoys the routine more than the score.
card.arts_persona: A steady reader, mostly history and narrative non-fiction: social history, books about ordinary working lives, the odd biography. He also reads some literary fiction recommended by his sister. He likes slow, well-made TV dramas and documentaries, and goes to the Connaught cinema in Worthing for smaller films now and then. His music taste is broad and he likes discovering older albums properly, front to back.
card.travel_persona: Prefers trips with something to learn. He has done a long weekend in Berlin with a mate, a week in Porto, and Ypres with his dad to see the war graves, which affected him more than he expected. He is a careful budgeter who books early and is happy staying in modest places. He would like to do a longer rail trip around central Europe once the deposit is sorted.
card.culinary_persona: His mum still does most of the dinners and he takes Thursdays and Sundays. He cooks decent curries from scratch, a slow-cooked chilli, and is working through a Middle Eastern cookbook. He takes packed lunches to work to save money. He has a weakness for a sausage roll from the bakery near the yard, and orders a proper fish and chips from the seafront on Fridays now and then.
skills: product knowledge of building materials and timber
quoting and pricing for trade accounts
managing a small rota and team
basic plumbing and DIY learned from his dad
card.career_goals: He would like to move up to branch manager within a few years, mainly for the better hours and pay. He also wonders, half-seriously, whether finishing an Open University degree could lead somewhere quieter, such as heritage, archives or teaching. He is realistic and won't jump without a plan, especially while saving for a flat.
card.voice: Friendly, mid-paced and fairly plain southern English with a mild Sussex/South East sound. Nothing broad. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal and sometimes 'mate' with people he knows. He uses 'erm' when gathering his thoughts and often says 'sort of' or 'kind of' when he is being careful not to overstate something. He tends to end with 'yeah' or 'you know' rather than flashier tags. He echoes the question back briefly before answering ('What do I do in the evenings? Erm, well...'). He is comfortable with a short pause and doesn't rush to fill silence. If he gets something wrong he corrects himself with a quick 'sorry, no, I mean...'. He says 'knackered' about the early starts.
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with a capital at the start and full stops. In quick answers he sometimes drops the final full stop. Apostrophes are usually correct, apart from the occasional slip on a phone. He doesn't use many abbreviations, maybe 'tbh' or 'etc'. He doesn't use emojis on a form. Answers are short and to the point, a bit longer if the question is about something he cares about.
card.with_strangers: Polite and a little reserved for the first few minutes, then warm once the conversation gets going. He asks a question back rather than talking about himself at length. He is modest about his job and his studying, and plays them down, but he is clearly interested in people. He comes across as genuine, with no attempt to impress.
small_things: the 6:30 starts and being knackered by Friday
a customer who ordered the wrong sheet sizes again
trying a new recipe on a Sunday
the seafront being windy on his ride
the train fares to London being daft
deeper_things: feeling a bit behind at 32, living back with his parents, even though he gets on well with them
regret about leaving university and quietly wanting to finish a degree
his last relationship ending because they wanted different things, and not rushing into anything new
worrying about his dad's knees and how long he can keep working
the Ypres trip making him think a lot about family history and his great-grandfather
card.webcam_photo: Head and shoulders, laptop camera slightly below eye level so the view angles up a little. Soft daylight from a window to his left, with a warm ceiling light also on. He has a pleasant, slightly tired face, light stubble, short mid-brown hair a bit flattened on one side, and no glasses. He is giving a small polite half-smile. He wears a navy crew-neck jumper over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a single-bedroom wall painted pale grey, with a pine bookshelf holding history paperbacks, a couple of Open University course books and a framed photo of a family beach trip. Part of a radiator with a drying towel is visible, and the corner of a single wardrobe door is half open.
